traits.note: FNA vol. 27, Niphotrichum (Ochyra and Bednarek-Ochyra; efloras, read 2026-11-05): plants loosely to densely caespitose or in extensive mats or patches, green, yellow- to greyish green, often hoary when dry (Greek nipha, snow, and trichos, hair); stems creeping to erect, often with short tuft-like branches; leaves erect-appressed when dry, usually awned; seta yellowish to blackish red. Typical values are N. ericoides, the roof taxon (Racomitrium canescens var. ericoides; same volume): extensive mats, yellow- or olive green, brown to blackish brown proximally; stems 3-8 cm, prostrate to ascending, pinnate; leaves appressed and slightly twisted dry, 2-3 x 0.9-1.2 mm, awns capillaceous or absent; seta dark to reddish brown 12-15 mm; capsule brown, long-cylindric, 1.5-2 mm; dry or intermittently moist sandy, gravelly soil and soil over rock, mostly non-calcareous. Bryophytes at Oregon State, rooftop study (nine Willamette Valley roofs; read 2026-11-05 as summarised in a search, the site itself blocked here): Dicranoweisia cirrata very abundant (45% occurrence), Bryum capillare abundant (33%), Racomitrium canescens var. ericoides abundant but infrequent (11%), able to form large mats; Dicranoweisia and Bryum capillare the only two species found on cedar shakes; most roofs had fewer than four species.

traits.height_typical_m.note: The depth of a mat of ascending stems 3-8 cm long: one to a few centimetres.

traits.hair_point_length_m.note: FNA gives awns but no length for N. ericoides; about a fifth of the leaf. Check against a measured flora.

traits.older_leaf_colour.note: FNA vol. 27, Niphotrichum ericoides (read 2026-11-05): brown to blackish brown proximally. The colour is ours for that brown.

traits.capsule_posture.note: FNA vol. 27, Grimmiaceae (read 2026-11-05): capsule usually erect; Niphotrichum seta erect.

traits.substrates.note: FNA's soil and rock, and roofs from OSU's survey.

traits.colony_spread_m_per_year.note: Estimate for a creeping mat with pinnate branches, below the pleurocarps'; to check against Glime, Bryophyte Ecology.

traits.leaf_colour.note: Hue measured: imagekit run moss-colour-2026-11-05 on batch moss-pnw-2026-11-05 (iNaturalist research-grade photos from Washington, about 20 a taxon, script moss_colour.py): the median linear r/g and b/g of the moss pixels (N. elongatum r/g 1.06, b/g 0.23, masked median only; the roof taxon N. ericoides had no Washington photos in the batch). Photos are exposed brighter than moss is, so only the hue is taken from them; the brightness is a green reflectance of 0.13, a lit leaf's, just above the 0.05-0.11 moss canopies reflect in the visible (Lovelock and Robinson 2002, Plant Cell Environ. 25: 1239, Antarctic Grimmia; moss biocrust albedo about 0.11 against 0.20 for bare soil, Sci. Total Environ. 2020), the canopy's own shade darkening the shell further.
